tasks.task: Write a cold email sequence for one buyer type

items.when: When you know the buyer type and need a short first email and follow-ups that each add something
Before writing, to compare three plans for the series, each with its first email
When you want a second full sequence with different timing and touches to set beside yours
When each email needs two or more subject lines to test
Before the sequence is loaded, to test claims, check the legal basics and tighten each email
When the first email explains the product and never gives a busy buyer a reason to change

tasks.task: Write personal first lines for a short list of leads

items.when: When you have up to 25 leads with a note on each and want one true opening line per person
When the whole email should sound like the sender and tie to something specific about each lead
When one account matters and you want an email, call opener and LinkedIn note from real signals
When batches go out every week and each should learn from the last batch's results
Before sending, to test each line about the lead against their own page text

tasks.task: Write a one-page pre-meeting account brief

items.when: When notes, filings, job posts and pages are gathered and need sorting into facts, signals and guesses
When little is gathered yet and you need a sourced research file on the company first
When the account is a listed company and the seller wants its numbers on one page
When talking points should tie to dated events such as results days or conferences
When you need recent news on the account with source links to check
Before the brief goes to the seller, so each fact has a dated source and guesses are marked

tasks.task: Build an ideal customer profile from past deals

items.when: When the client has won, lost and churned deals and says they sell to everyone
When you have what each customer paid and how long they stayed, to find the top fifth
When closed deals should show which traits go with wins and which with losses
When the profile needs the person as well as the company: pains, goals and what they tried
When the profile feels settled, to hear the best case that it describes the wrong buyer

tasks.task: Score and tier a lead list

items.when: When the profile is agreed and a pasted list needs scores, red flags and tier cut-offs
When leads have activity as well as fit and both should count toward the tier
When you want a second ranking by account, with reasons, to compare with your tiers
When the team wants a simple grade a rep can apply in seconds
Before the scored sheet goes back, to catch broken formulas and rows scored twice

tasks.task: Build and clean a prospect list

items.when: When you start from the profile and want a list, a ranking and checked first messages
When you need accounts that fit, with the reason each one is on the list
When records lack company size, role or contact details needed for routing and outreach
Before any send, to flag bad, role-based and throwaway addresses
When contact details must be pulled from several sources into one list
When you need contacts by role and company and will email from the same account

tasks.task: Plan an outbound campaign from profile to held meetings

items.when: When the client wants more meetings, opens a new segment or has too few early deals
When you need who to target, which buying signals to watch and a multi-channel order of touches
When the choice is few accounts worked deeply or many worked lightly, to see both with numbers
When more than one person is involved and roles and lead flow must be set
When the same person is asked to prospect, close and look after accounts

tasks.task: Write a cold call script with gatekeeper and voicemail lines

items.when: When you need a one-page script: opener, two fit questions, the ask and replies to brush-offs
When you want a second script with its own opener and voicemail to compare
When reps freeze on the first line, to get a ten-word opener, two spares and a test
When a brush-off keeps coming up and you need what it means and a reply
When the script is drafted, to cut lines that pressure or pretend a prior relationship
When the script is fine and the real problem is that calls do not get made

tasks.task: Plan a calling session and the booking confirmations

items.when: When the session needs its script, the meeting ask and what to send once a slot is agreed
When you need a protected call block, a quick research batch and one reason to call each lead
When booked meetings should go through a page with prep emails and reminders
When the team should rehearse the opener before the block, planned minute by minute

tasks.task: Write LinkedIn connection and follow-up messages

items.when: When each connection note should open with something true about that person
When you need who to comment on, connection notes and a plan, all sent by hand
When the note is forgettable, to get three versions of the same line to choose from
Before sending, to test what the note claims about the person and tighten it

tasks.task: Write replies to the answers outreach gets back

items.when: When replies such as not now, send info or wrong person get a different answer each time
When the doubts repeat and you want one answer with proof for each
When you want a second set of replies to likely objections for one prospect
When a reply pushes for yes and should let a no move things on instead
Before the scripts are saved, to find any line that presses or overclaims

tasks.task: Write first replies and routing rules for inbound enquiries

items.when: When enquiries by form, missed call, chat or demo request wait hours for an answer
When setting up the daily routine, or a new enquiry source is added
When you want a second draft that qualifies the enquiry and offers real meeting times
When leads sit unassigned and need an owner by rule and a handoff note
When several enquiries arrive at once and must be ranked by fit and urgency
Before a template is saved, to cut it and check it has one next step

tasks.task: Write qualification questions and a call-back script

items.when: When new enquiries need a call-back script with fit questions and a booked next step
When you need the few questions that show whether this enquiry is worth a meeting
When you want a second way to open the call-back to compare
After a round of calls, to see which leads made a real commitment and what to ask next
When the questions tick boxes for the seller and uncover nothing about the buyer's problem

tasks.task: Write a follow-up series for enquiries that go quiet

items.when: Before writing, to compare three plans for the two weeks of follow-up
When one email must become four, each with a new reason, one ask and a stop rule
When quiet leads should get useful information first and the ask second
When a warm lead stopped replying and you want to know which kind of stall it is
Before the series is loaded, to check each email is short with one ask

tasks.task: Write the hand-off note from SDR to closer

items.when: When a meeting is booked and the closer needs why the buyer said yes, in their own words
When the closer also needs a one-page brief on the account before the meeting
When several people at the account are involved and the closer needs who matters
When the emails and calls behind the booking are not yet in the CRM

tasks.task: Check outreach rules before a campaign goes live

items.when: Before a new sequence, calling block or text campaign, or when contacting a new country
When you must show which contacts gave real permission and where each address came from
When you are unsure which marketing and privacy rules apply where the buyers are
When each email should also pass the basics: who you are, why them and how to opt out

tasks.task: Set up sending so cold email reaches the inbox

items.when: When emails land in spam and the sending domain's records need setting up
When you need the sending setup that goes with the sequence: volumes, gaps and inboxes
Before each batch, to remove addresses that will bounce and hurt the sender's standing

tasks.task: Review outreach results and plan the next test

items.when: When a campaign has run and you compare meetings held with the plan
When two openers or offers should be tested fairly with one change and a winner rule
When replies are few or weak and the offer itself needs three changes to try
When the next batch should be written from what the last one earned

tasks.task: Sharpen the reason to reply

items.when: When there is nothing useful to offer a cold buyer except a meeting
When the outreach needs what the buyer gains and proof from a similar customer
When you want a version of the message that leads with the belief, then how, then what
When the message could come from any rival, to see if buyers will only compare on price

tasks.task: Follow up leads from a trade show or event

items.when: When you have a note on each person you met and want an opening line for each
When attendee notes must become follow-ups grouped by what each person asked for
When the follow-up will run to several emails and you want three ways to plan it
Before sending, to check each claim about the conversation and tighten the email

tasks.task: Map the stakeholders in one target account

items.when: When the map should start from sourced facts on who holds which role
When you need the people, their influence and mood, and who is missing
When the account is large and needs a full plan around the map

always.when: When any message or brief states a fact about a prospect, so it has a dated source
Before templates are loaded, to catch typos and a name or company spelt two ways

helpers.when: When routing, scoring or stages must be built into the CRM, not kept on a sheet
When sending set-up, list health or inbox placement is the real problem
When reps need battlecards, call coaching or a playbook behind the scripts
When outbound needs content, ads or events working alongside it
When outreach enters a new country or uses calls and texts with strict consent rules
When the ideal customer profile needs outside market data, not only past deals

gaps: No library item checks outreach against email, call and text rules by country, including do-not-call lists
No library item writes gatekeeper lines or a set of voicemail drops as its own piece
No library item writes meeting confirmations, reminders and a no-show recovery message
No library item writes the hand-off note from the person who booked the meeting to the closer
No library item sets speed-to-lead targets and routing rules by enquiry source
No library item reads outbound results by step: reply rate, positive replies, meetings booked and held
No library item writes first replies for web chat, missed calls and call-backs
No library item plans a team calling session with dial, connect and booking targets
No library item plans text or WhatsApp outreach to leads with consent checks
No library item plans how fast to raise cold email volume on a new sending domain
